packages.label: דְּבַשׁ וְאִשָּׁה
packages.reason: The only explicit identity (bechina) statement in Torah #199 is the gematria equation: 'דְּבַשׁ בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא אִשָּׁה' — honey and woman share the same numerical value (306). The Rebbe cites this as a foundational equivalence grounding the entire teaching's mechanism: the taste of sweetness in Torah IS the bechina of דבש, and since דבש = אשה, that sweetness acts directly on the spiritual domain of אשה (wife, woman). The polarity is neutral: both דבש and אשה are natural/relational concepts that are neither inherently holy nor evil. They function here as the shared pivot between the eitza-domain of Torah-study and the eitza-domain of marital life. The teaching does not assign positive or negative valence to דבש or אשה themselves — they are the structural link through which the practice (feeling sweetness in Torah) operates on the protective domain.

The bechina equation is stated explicitly in line 3: 'כִּי דְּבַשׁ בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא אִשָּׁה כַּמּוּבָא בַּכְּתָבִים'. The Rebbe cites kabbalistic writings (כתבים = the Ari's writings) as the source for this equation.

The gematria proof: ד+ב+ש = 4+2+300 = 306; א+ש+ה = 1+300+5 = 306. Equal gematria in Rebbe Nachman's methodology functions as a bechina — the two words share the same essential numerical-spiritual root.

This two-node package is the smallest possible package; the entire Torah's structure radiates from this single bechina pivot. The teaching exists to communicate one thing: because of this identity (דבש = אשה), sweetness in Torah sweetens the judgment of one's wife.
